office_does: The three county commissioners are Lewis County's legislative body: they adopt the budget, pass ordinances and oversee county departments. District 3 candidates are nominated in East and south Lewis County, but every county voter elects them in November.
race_blurb: Republican incumbent Scott Brummer, first elected in 2022, faces Republican PUD Commissioner Mike Hadaller of Salkum. Brummer led the district-only primary 33.6% to 31.7%. Both oppose a public safety tax for now. They split on the proposed Chehalis River flow-through dam and on how the county is run: Hadaller wants audits of every funded agency and an end to the county manager position.

candidates.summary: District 3 commissioner since 2022, former state fish biologist, senior pastor in Ethel and farm-feed business owner, running on his record of budget restraint and flood-control work.
highlights: Says the board took the allowed property-tax increase only once in four budgets [S3][S2]
Chairs the Chehalis Basin board and supports the proposed flow-through flood dam near Pe Ell [S1][S3][S4]
'Not sold' on a public safety tax until a new sheriff rebuilds trust [S3][S4]
Voted against allowing cannabis sales in unincorporated Lewis County [S5]
Would not cut deputies to end the road-fund transfer to the sheriff [S6]

experience.basis: Incumbent running explicitly on his record, budget votes and regional board chairmanships.

taxes.basis: Record and repeated statements of keeping property-tax increases to a minimum; hesitant on, but not closed to, a dedicated public safety tax.

spending.basis: Says the board has kept spending down and made hard choices, but refuses to cut deputy positions funded by the road-fund transfer.

safety.basis: Pledges support for law enforcement, defended the county's syringe ordinance and voted against cannabis sales over youth access.

candidates.summary: Lewis County PUD commissioner since 2022 and board president, a Salkum resident from a longtime East County logging family, running to put the district's voice first and audit county spending.
highlights: Wants every agency that receives county tax money open to audit, the sheriff included [S3]
Would eliminate the $177,000 county manager position [S2]
Opposes a public safety tax before audits and opposes the proposed flow-through dam [S2]
Promises an open-door policy, expedited permitting and a crackdown on drug houses [S1][S3]

experience.basis: Challenges the incumbent on change and East County representation, with one term on the PUD board as his elected record.

spending.basis: Calls for audits of every county-funded entity, eliminating the county manager and 'tighten the belt' budgeting.

taxes.basis: Opposes a public safety tax until departments are audited and favors 'getting government out of the way', while allowing that roads and safety must be paid for.

safety.basis: Enforcement framing on burglaries, drug dealers and drug houses; opposed cannabis sales in unincorporated areas.
